semantic_changes: Seventh case set added around the already-settled scenario; each case has its own admission, result event name and comparison, and the derived boolean `ok_claimed_entry_absent` makes the single predicate 'no success claim for an absent entry' evaluable for every tick period.

scope.description: Tick-period sweep of the already-established lost-entry scenario, run as one invocation of seven cases over the same in-process cluster shape (three OmniPaxos actors, in-memory transport, majority quorum, batch_size 1, node 1 forced into the leader role, egress 1 ms so the re-synchronisation round trip is about 2 ms). Case A is the no-partition control at 2 ms; case B repeats the partition at 2 ms; cases C, D, E, F and G use the identical partition and differ only in tick period (80, 4, 8, 16 and 40 ms). Each case emits its result under its own event name and reports the resolved variant, the assigned index, the decided entry at that index, whether it equals the submitted value, and a derived boolean `ok_claimed_entry_absent` whose operands stay visible.
assumptions: Message loss/partition is a permitted fault; whole messages are dropped in the transport with the receiving side still draining, so no backpressure is introduced.

Only the tick period differs between the partition cases; node ids, priorities, quorum, batch size, egress period, election and resend tick counts and the append_notify timeout are otherwise equal (resend_message_tick_timeout is 5 ticks for A-E and 4 for G).
The crate's `RuntimeConfig::default()` tick period is 10 ms, which is why the 8, 16 and 40 ms cases matter for the deployment question.
Each node is a real OmniPaxos instance with MemoryStorage driven only through the public actor handle.
excluded: Any claim about entries other than the submitted values 11 (origin) and 22 (new leader).
Any claim about the exact tick/RTT threshold beyond the sampled points 2, 4, 8, 16, 40 and 80 ms.
Any claim about follower-origin assignments, batching above 1, flexible quorums or crash recovery.

basis.prefix: Same scenario as the settled runtime probe, run once per case. Build three OmniPaxos instances (pids 1..3, configuration_id 1, MemoryStorage, batch_size 1, election_tick_timeout 3, node 1 leader_priority 1), spawn each through spawn_actor with a tokio-backed AsyncRuntime adapter at the case's tick period and a 1 ms egress period, and wire outgoing_messages() to the receiver's handle_incoming() through a transport task that consults a per-direction block set. Elect node 1 and emit the admission event (mode, setup, origin 1, submitted_value 11, tick period) once all three nodes report it as the accepted leader after four election timeouts. Case A: await handles[1].append_notify(TestEntry(11)) with no partition. Cases B-G: block (1,2) and (1,3) both ways, spawn handles[1].append_notify(TestEntry(11)), sleep one tick period, wait until nodes 2 and 3 report a leader other than 1, await handles[new_leader].append_notify(TestEntry(22)), then unblock and await the origin's future. Emit new_leader_elected, new_leader_append and the mode-specific outcome event carrying resolved, assigned_idx, entry_at_assigned_idx, entry_equals_submitted (only when the index was observed), entry_present_matches_submitted and ok_claimed_entry_absent.
basis.responsibility: The decisive inputs come from the target: the actor assigns the index from its own local accept as leader, stores only (index, ballot), and `drain_notifiers` - reachable only from the tick branch - answers `Ok(assigned_idx)` from the local decided index before it evaluates the ballot-change arm, with no comparison against the entry occupying that index.

comparisons.description: Control at 2 ms with no partition: no success claim for an absent entry.
Partition at 2 ms: predicted holds (Superseded is the documented arm).
Partition at 80 ms: previously violated; predicated to stay violated.
Partition at 4 ms: predicted holds (tick period still shorter than the re-synchronisation round trip).
Partition at 8 ms: predicted violated (false success at the default-like tick period).
